messages:
sara: FYI customer acme-realtime flagged an invoice delta vs dashboard: billed ~12,340 tokens higher for Feb 26. They say dashboard served tokens look normal. Any quick theory?

aj: Oof. First guess: prefetch/prefix KV warmups being metered but not counted as served? Seen this with ctbatcher prefetch windows before. Do we have a repro trace or request IDs?

sara: They attached a trace id: trace_0x9f2b and example request ids: req-88a, req-88b, req-913. Logs show repeated prefetch calls at 03:14:22 UTC.

devin: Can you paste the rough log snippet? If prefetch fires on warmups it can allocate billable tokens (tokenization + upstream calls) but never surface in served token aggregates if cached hits later.

sara: Paste from their export: ```
[03:14:22.112] prefetch: model=gpt-medium, key=prefix:/org/ACME/ctx/123, tokens=256, trace=trace_0x9f2b
[03:14:22.116] batcher: assigned to ctbatch-7, window_ms=80
[03:14:22.140] kvcache: hit=false, storing key=prefix:/org/ACME/ctx/123
[03:14:22.210] request req-88a: served=32 tokens
```

maria: That looks like prefetch warmed a 256-token prefix, which would be counted as billed at prefetch time. If later requests hit cached KV, dashboard served tokens show only the 32 tokens returned per request. Billing counts the prefetch work.

aj: Important to confirm meter source: invoice uses the metering pipeline which consumes metered_token events emitted by the runtime. We had a bug where prefetch emitted events with metered_source="prefetch" but were filtered out from dashboard served_token aggregates (dashboard only sums "served" events).

devin: I can run a quick query against the metering bucket for that org and window. Give me 10m.

billing-bot: Query queued: SELECT SUM(metered_tokens) as billed, SUM(served_tokens) as served FROM metering WHERE org='ACME' AND ts BETWEEN 1677410000 AND 1677413600 GROUP BY hour; job_id=Q-7334

aj: While Devin runs the query: customer also mentioned continuous batching was recently rolled to 0-100ms windows on Dedicated. That increases prefetch density — could explain spike.

devin: Results: billed=1,234,560 tokens, served=1,222,220 tokens, delta=12,340 tokens (matches their invoice). Breakdown: ~98% of delta attributed to metered_source IN ('prefetch','warmup').

sara: OK that's pretty convincing. Customer wants either credit or an explanation. Can we confirm this behavior is documented anywhere?

maria: We have docs that say prefetching is billable but we hide prefetch in the per-request served view to avoid double-counting when cache hits occur. But the wording is subtle — support should explain prefetch is billed when it executes even if subsequent requests hit cache.

aj: Action items: (1) Offer ACME a one-time invoice adjustment for Feb while we improve visibility in the console. (2) Add a metering breakdown in the console for metered_source dimension (prefetch, served, kv_write, kv_read). (3) Add a short KB entry calling out continuous batching config impact.

ops_oncall: Quick mitigation if customer wants to avoid future surprise charges: disable prefetch for their org or reduce batcher.prefetch_window_ms to 0. Also can flip kvcache.prefetch_on_write=false in Dedicated.

sara: ACME prefers to keep perf, they'll accept a one-time credit and want more transparency. I'll draft the response with suggested mitigations + docs link.

maria: I'll own the console change spec to surface metered_source breakdowns — filing an RFC this week.

aj: I'll add an internal alert when metered_source='prefetch' exceeds threshold to catch big warmup storms.

sara: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer and attach our repro notes. :thumbsup:
